## Intro

This document goes over the steps to prepare and model *Nyctanassa violacea* eBird data, largely based on the tutorial provided by [Strimas-Mackey et al. (2023)](https://ebird.github.io/ebird-best-practices/).

The code below checks and install required packages as needed:

```{r eval=F,echo=F,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
pkgs <- c('tidyverse','rnaturalerthdata','terra','auk')
  
for (i in pkgs){
  if (!(requireNamespace(pkg,quietly = TRUE))){
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}
```

## eBird data

First step is to import eBird data into R. Data comes in two formats: observations (i.e., each row is one observation for that species) and checklists (i.e., each row is an checklist for which that species was observed). Both will be used throughout this document to estimate final metrics reflecting species presence and abundance.

We will use `auk` functions `read_ebd()` and `read_sampling()` to import observations and checklists, respectively:

```{r eval=F,echo=F,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
observations <- read_ebd('data/')

samp_filt <- samp %>%
  filter(all_species_reported,
         between(year(observation_date), 2000, 2025),
         observation_type %in% c("Stationary", "Traveling"),
         duration_minutes <= 360,
         effort_distance_km <= 10,
         number_observers <= 10)
```

Exploration of final filtered data:
--Breeding information
--Individual age

--Temporal distribution of points throughout the year (to visualize yearly migration and breeding seasons)
--Mapping sampling effort based on number of observers, checklist, effort in km/h, etc.
